what: Crown Castle owns more than 40,000 mobile phone towers across the United States and leases space on them to mobile operators. It has agreed to sell its fibre and small cell business to focus on towers alone.
customers: The large US mobile operators, which lease antenna space under long-term contracts.
money: long-term leases of antenna space to mobile operators
fibre routes and small cell nodes
moat: Tower sites with planning permission and existing tenants, where adding a second or third operator to the same structure costs almost nothing and nearly all of it is profit.
risks: Debt of about $23 billion against almost no cash
Mobile operator consolidation means fewer tenants per tower
It cut its dividend when it restructured around towers
Revenue has fallen about 15% a year over three years as the fibre business was wound down
opportunities: Gross margin of 97% on tower leases, because the structure is already built
Selling the fibre business raises cash to cut debt
Leases typically include annual price increases written into the contract
watch: Organic tower revenue growth and the completion of the fibre sale.
